title: Why You Still Remember Year 9 Chemistry

pre.en: How many people remember Alan Price's talk from last year?
pre.zh: 有几个人记得 Alan Price 去年讲了什么？

intro: 一场晚间公开讲座：心理学老师 Alan Price 讲「为什么有些课我们一辈子都记得」。讲座是说给人听的：开头打招呼、先预告要讲什么，中间用 Which brings me to … 转话题，结尾一句俏皮话收场。读的时候留意 If only：比 wish 语气更强的「要是……就好了」。

sentences.en: Good evening, everyone, and thanks for coming out on a wet Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 各位晚上好，谢谢大家下雨的星期二还出门来听。

sentences.en: I'm Alan Price, and I teach psychology here.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alan Price，在这儿教心理学。

sentences.en: So, first I'll ask you a question, then I'll explain the research, and then I'll tell you about Mr Jenkins.
sentences.zh: 我先问大家一个问题，再讲讲研究结果，最后讲讲 Jenkins 老师。

sentences.en: Think of one lesson from school — the first one that comes to mind — and shout it out.
sentences.zh: 想一节上学时的课，脑子里冒出来的第一节就行，大声说出来。

sentences.en: Nobody's said "a normal Thursday", have they?
sentences.zh: 没有人说「一个普通的星期四」，对吧？

sentences.en: Personally, I wish I'd listened more in history, but I can't remember a single lesson.
sentences.zh: 我自己吧，真后悔当年历史课没好好听，现在一节都想不起来了。

sentences.en: Well, a lesson sticks in your mind when it makes you feel something: surprise, fear, even embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 其实，一节课要是能让你有点感觉——惊讶、害怕，甚至是难堪——你就会一直记得它。

sentences.en: Students who take notes by hand remember more than students who type.
sentences.zh: 手写笔记的学生，比打字的记得多。

sentences.en: And going over your notes the night before an exam doesn't actually help much.
sentences.zh: 考试前一晚把笔记过一遍，其实没多大用。

sentences.en: I can see some of you pulling a face.
sentences.zh: 我看到有些人在皱眉头了。

sentences.en: If only I'd known this at sixteen.
sentences.zh: 要是我十六岁时就知道这些该多好。

sentences.en: Which brings me to Mr Jenkins, my Year 9 chemistry teacher.
sentences.zh: 这就说到 Jenkins 老师了，他是我初三的化学老师。

sentences.en: I had second thoughts about telling this story, because he still lives round the corner.
sentences.zh: 讲不讲这个故事，我犹豫过，因为他还住在附近。

sentences.en: He might be here tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚他说不定就坐在台下。

sentences.en: In 1994, he was showing us an experiment when he accidentally set fire to a bench.
sentences.zh: 1994 年，他给我们做一个实验，结果不小心把实验台点着了。

sentences.en: It didn't go as described in the textbook, and we couldn't believe our eyes.
sentences.zh: 实验完全没按课本上写的来，我们都看傻了眼。

sentences.en: He made an impression on the whole class, and after that, he held our attention with every topic.
sentences.zh: 全班都对他印象深刻，从那以后，他讲什么我们都听得聚精会神。

sentences.en: The school was short-staffed, so we had him for three years.
sentences.zh: 学校缺老师，所以他教了我们整整三年。

sentences.en: Years later, I found out he hadn't got permission to do it.
sentences.zh: 很多年后我才知道，那个实验他根本没得到批准。

sentences.en: Apparently, the school just learned to live with the black mark on the bench.
sentences.zh: 听说实验台上那块黑印，学校也就一直将就着没管。

sentences.en: If only I'd had a camera that day.
sentences.zh: 要是那天我带了相机就好了。

sentences.en: If only every teacher could do that — though perhaps without the fire.
sentences.zh: 要是每个老师都能做到这样就好了——当然，最好别着火。

sentences.en: And if only I could make my own lectures that memorable.
sentences.zh: 要是我自己的讲座也能让人记得这么牢就好了。

sentences.en: Before you go, hands up if you remember what I talked about here last year.
sentences.zh: 大家走之前，记得我去年在这儿讲了什么的，请举手。

sentences.en: Nobody?
sentences.zh: 没人？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 这就对了。

sentences.en: Neither do I.
sentences.zh: 我自己也不记得。

cards.note: p 不发音，读作 /saɪˈkɒlədʒi/；心理学家 psychologist。
if something comes to mind, you suddenly think of it or remember it
cards.tip: 主语是被想起的东西，不是人：Nothing comes to mind，不说 I come to mind。
cards.example: When I think of summer, long evenings in the garden come to mind.

cards.zh: 让人一直记得；印在脑子里
cards.note: if something sticks in your mind, you remember it for a long time
cards.tip: 主语是被记住的事；stick 的过去式、过去分词是 stuck。
cards.example: One thing he said in that meeting has stuck in my mind.

cards.note: 形容词 embarrassed（人觉得尴尬）、embarrassing（事情让人尴尬）。拼写注意双 r、双 s。
to write down information while you are listening to someone or reading something
cards.tip: notes 用复数；动词用 take，不用 write：take notes，也说 make notes。
cards.example: Can someone take notes during the meeting?

cards.note: to look at or study something again carefully
cards.tip: 后面接要检查、复习的东西：go over your notes / the figures；go over to 是「走过去」。
cards.example: Let's go over the plan one more time before the client arrives.

cards.zh: （因为不喜欢）皱起脸；露出嫌弃的表情
cards.note: to make an expression with your face to show that you do not like something
ch 读 /k/；化学家 chemist，英式里 chemist 还是「药店」。
to start to have doubts about a decision you have made
cards.tip: thoughts 用复数；对什么犹豫用 about；on second thoughts 是「再一想」。
cards.example: I had second thoughts about the flat when I saw the kitchen.

cards.note: 做实验是 do / carry out an experiment。
= by accident；反义 on purpose（故意）。
公园长椅也叫 bench；实验室里的台子是 lab bench。
the same as someone said or wrote it would be
cards.tip: 常见于网购和评价：not as described（和描述不符）；这里借来说实验「没按课本写的来」。
cards.example: The hotel room was exactly as described on the website.

cards.note: to be very surprised by something you see
to make someone notice and remember you
cards.tip: 可以加形容词：make a good / bad / big impression on sb；第一印象是 first impression。
cards.example: She made a great impression on the interview panel.

cards.note: to keep someone interested so that they keep listening or watching
cards.tip: sb's 跟着人称变：hold our / their attention；「引起注意」是 get / catch sb's attention。
cards.example: It's hard to hold children's attention for more than ten minutes.

cards.note: to not have enough workers
to be told officially that you can do something

cards.zh: 学会接受（不理想的情况）
cards.note: to accept something that is not perfect because you cannot change it
cards.tip: 说的是无法改变、只好接受的事；英式过去式也可写 learnt。
cards.example: The neighbours' dog barks all day, but we've learned to live with it.

cards.note: 来自 memory；a memorable day 难忘的一天。
